verdicts.quote: a ticket waits on its requester while it is `resolved`

every ticket that is `resolved`, whose latest resolve time (`at` of its latest audit entry with `changes.status.to = 'resolved'`; not `ticket.updated`) is at least 7 days (604800000 ms) before the clock's now
resolved again later, its 7 days count from the new resolve, and it can be reminded once for that resolution.
a ticket reopened (resolved -> open) before day 7 gets no reminder
verdicts.missing: The status rule covers transitions and ordinary edits. It leaves unspecified what action counts as a requester response when there is no reply endpoint.

verdicts.quote: subject `[T-0001] Waiting for your reply` and a body containing the ticket title and the number of days waiting (7)
verdicts.missing: The recipient is the requester field. The specification leaves open how to deliver to a free-text value that is not an address and what action the body asks the requester to take.

verdicts.quote: the resolved notice already says "Reply within 7 days to reopen it"
verdicts.missing: The reminder is due when the stated reply period expires. The specification gives no instruction for how the requester can act then or how the reminder should describe that deadline.

verdicts.quote: with `WORKER_INTERVAL_MS=0` no reminder is enqueued by the service on its own (no timer, no side effect of a request).
running the job again (also after the reminder is delivered/sent, and at 30 days) enqueues nothing more and appends no second `ticket.reminded`.
verdicts.missing: The persistent audit entry prevents another enqueue. What prevents a delivery retry from sending the already queued notification twice is unspecified.

verdicts.quote: the worker, on each tick, finds every ticket that is `resolved`
verdicts.missing: The worker selects eligible tickets each tick and saves the event and audit entry together. Whether it checks eligibility again or holds it stable between selection and enqueue is unspecified.

verdicts.quote: an event of this type is never dead for want of a template.
verdicts.missing: The audit rule suppresses another reminder after enqueue. The specification leaves the retry and dead-state policy for other delivery failures and the timing of template validation undecided.

verdicts.quote: on each tick, finds every ticket that is `resolved`, whose latest resolve time (`at` of its latest audit entry with `changes.status.to = 'resolved'`; not `ticket.updated`) is at least 7 days (604800000 ms) before the clock's now
resolved again later, its 7 days count from the new resolve, and it can be reminded once for that resolution.
verdicts.missing: The cycle resets the clock and allowance. How the outbox key distinguishes resolutions of the same ticket when an older reminder is pending is unspecified.

verdicts.quote: on each tick, finds every ticket that is `resolved`, whose latest resolve time (`at` of its latest audit entry with `changes.status.to = 'resolved'`; not `ticket.updated`) is at least 7 days (604800000 ms) before the clock's now
appends one audit entry `ticket.reminded`, actor `system`, empty `changes`, in the same store step (saved together).
the data file's version and readability of existing data files
verdicts.missing: The design adds no field requiring a default. It leaves unspecified whether loading must reject malformed reminder audit data and identify the offending field.

verdicts.quote: appends one audit entry `ticket.reminded`, actor `system`, empty `changes`
verdicts.missing: Whether appending the audit entry changes ticket.updated is unspecified.

verdicts.quote: no new ticket status, field, API endpoint or configuration variable
verdicts.missing: The threshold is fixed and the worker sends automatically. Whether anyone can manually trigger or suppress an individual reminder, and with what authority, is unspecified.

verdicts.quote: with `WORKER_INTERVAL_MS=0` no reminder is enqueued by the service on its own
verdicts.missing: The existing worker interval controls scheduling. Its default and the validation error for an invalid value are unspecified.

verdicts.quote: Observed in `store.outboxReport()` / GET /admin/outbox and `store.history`.
the job runs before deliver-outbox in the same tick so a due reminder goes out in that tick or the next.
verdicts.missing: Each tick processes every eligible ticket. The specification gives no elapsed-time limit from threshold to delivery or cost bound that keeps a large scan from blocking delivery.

verdicts.quote: Every existing API response, the lifecycle, `list --raw` column positions, the weekly report, the data file's version and readability of existing data files, and the `ticket.created` / `ticket.resolved` notifications are unchanged.
verdicts.missing: The preservation rule names raw column positions but leaves other command-line output and CLI list-filter behaviour unspecified.
